title: Close Story Analysis Workflow Stage 4 Certification Gaps

story.so_that: the Story Analysis Workflow can demonstrate auditable, safe, reliable end-to-end operation and qualify for Stage 4 certification
story.as_a: Stage 4 certification owner for the Story Analysis Workflow
story.i_want: to close the identified agent-quality, guardrail, punch-out, success-reporting, and audit-trail gaps

target_persona.role: Engineering owner responsible for certification readiness and evidence

journey.before: Reviews certification criteria, implementation, design artifacts, evaluation results, and existing run logs to identify unsupported claims and missing controls.
journey.during: Coordinates agent-quality improvements, adds explicit workflow guardrails and escalation behavior, runs representative scenarios, and consolidates execution evidence.
journey.after: Audits the generated reports and logs, calculates the end-to-end success rate, and submits traceable evidence for Stage 4 examination.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Make the Story Analysis Workflow demonstrably compliant with all five Stage 4 certification criteria
inputs: Stage 4 certification criteria and quality thresholds
Skill output artifacts and their JSON schemas
Per-attempt activity logs and raw Devin ATIF exports
outputs: Stage 3 certification evidence for all four agents
Explicit startup, between-step, adversarial, and post-grader guardrail outcomes
Tested ambiguity punch-out and bypass-rejection evidence
Representative end-to-end benchmark records and an aggregate success rate
A consolidated workflow report for every completed run
Structured logs that distinguish automated failure from human decisions
state_changes: A workflow may fail before extraction when its source is not a valid Markdown document
Each activity handoff becomes contingent on artifact existence and schema validity
Ambiguous activity or guardrail outcomes may transition the workflow to an awaiting-human state
Human accept, retry, abort, timeout, and automated failure become separately auditable outcomes
Completed runs persist consolidated metadata, step outcomes, usage, and cost data
Certification evidence changes from partial and scattered to consolidated and reviewable
side_effects: Additional workflow, activity, validation, escalation, and human-decision log events
Additional report and benchmark artifacts under repository-controlled evidence locations
Potentially increased workflow latency and activity count from explicit guardrail nodes
Potential human notifications when ambiguity or exhausted retries trigger punch-out

ui: Story-analysis CLI status/query output may expose guardrail, failure-origin, and human-wait states
api: Cadence StoryAnalysisWorkflow input and result contracts
Cadence human_response Signal validation and handling
database: No application database schema change is identified
Cadence persists workflow state and event history in the existing local SQLite-backed stack
Filesystem report and log artifacts require deterministic paths and retention expectations

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All four Story Analysis agents have linked, reproducible real-work evaluation evidence at or above the 95% Stage 3 quality bar, and the observed manual-correction rate is reported.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the latest representative real-work evaluations for extract-story-intent, analyze-story, grade-story-analysis, and repair-story-analysis, when the certification artifact is generated, then every agent has a reproducible score of at least 95% and the manual-correction and escalation rates are stated with their sample size.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A valid Markdown story completes the automated workflow through explicit guardrails and produces all required artifacts and a consolidated report.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an accessible Markdown story and successful skill outputs, when the workflow runs, then a startup guardrail passes, every between-step artifact guardrail passes, the post-grader guardrail confirms the intent, analysis, and grade artifacts, and the run completes with a report covering every executed step.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The workflow rejects invalid, missing, inaccessible, or schema-invalid inputs and intermediate artifacts before scheduling a dependent skill activity.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a missing, inaccessible, non-Markdown, nonexistent, empty, or schema-invalid source or intermediate artifact, when its guardrail runs, then the dependent activity is not scheduled, the workflow fails safely or punches out only when ambiguity is explicitly classified, and the exact failing guardrail and artifact are logged.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Invalid or absent human responses cannot bypass an awaiting-human workflow, while valid retry, accept, and abort decisions produce distinct deterministic outcomes.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a live workflow awaiting a human signal, when no signal arrives before the configured boundary or a caller sends an unsupported, stale, duplicate, or unauthorized decision, then the workflow remains safely blocked, times out according to policy, or rejects the signal without treating it as valid; and when an authorized operator sends retry, accept, or abort, then the corresponding transition and decision origin are recorded.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Ambiguity raised during an activity or guardrail uses the ACTIVITY_FLAGGED_AMBIGUITY punch-out path and is proven by automated and recorded-run evidence.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an activity or guardrail returns an explicitly ambiguous result, when the engine evaluates it, then the workflow enters an awaiting-human state with reason ACTIVITY_FLAGGED_AMBIGUITY, accepts only a valid decision, and stores both integration-test evidence and at least one recorded execution trace.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Escalate ambiguous analysis to a human

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every completed workflow writes a schema-valid consolidated report containing run metadata, all attempts and steps, final status and origin, model settings, durations, artifacts, token totals, and cost representation.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow reaches passed, human_resolved, or failed, when completion processing runs, then exactly one schema-valid report is written atomically for that run and includes workflow_id, run_id, story_document, final_status, attempt_count, failure or resolution origin, and one ordered record for every activity attempt with step, activity_type, model, permission_mode, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cached_tokens, cost_usd or an explicit unavailable value, duration_ms, and output_path.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Audit a workflow from one report

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The end-to-end success metric is computed over a visible representative sample and remains traceable to individual reports.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given recorded runs for happy path, one repair, exhausted repair with human accept, exhausted repair with human abort, automated guardrail failure, and ambiguity punch-out, when aggregation runs, then it publishes the metric formula, numerator, denominator, sample window, status counts, manual-intervention rate, and links each observation to its workflow report without double-counting retries as separate runs.
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Measure workflow reliability across real runs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Boundary-sized histories, maximum repair attempts, and the human-response timeout boundary produce bounded, complete, and deterministic reports.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a run at the configured maximum repair count, maximum expected step or attempt count, or exact human-response timeout boundary, when it terminates, then no extra repair or wait occurs, all attempts appear once in order, totals do not overflow or become negative, and the terminal status follows the configured boundary rule.

edge_cases.criterion: Null, empty, whitespace-only, nonexistent, directory, non-Markdown, and inaccessible story_document values
edge_cases.gherkin: Given any null, empty, whitespace-only, nonexistent, directory, non-Markdown, or unreadable story_document value, when startup validation runs, then extraction is not scheduled and a sanitized deterministic validation failure is recorded.

edge_cases.criterion: Very long paths and Markdown documents at the supported size boundary
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a valid path and Markdown document at the declared maximum supported sizes, when the workflow runs, then validation and processing either complete within configured limits or fail with an explicit size-limit result without partial downstream execution.

edge_cases.criterion: Unicode, emoji, spaces, and shell-special characters in paths and document content
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a valid Markdown story whose path or content contains Unicode, emoji, spaces, or shell-special characters, when the workflow runs, then the exact path is handled without command injection or lossy normalization and report JSON remains valid UTF-8.

edge_cases.criterion: First run with no existing log, report, benchmark, or certification artifact directories
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a correctly configured writable workspace with no prior run artifacts, when the first workflow executes, then required artifact directories and one complete report are created without relying on historical data.
edge_cases.jtbd: Record the first certified workflow run

edge_cases.criterion: Partial report write or process interruption at workflow completion
edge_cases.gherkin: Given report generation is interrupted after completion starts, when the run is inspected or recovery executes, then no truncated file is treated as a valid report and regeneration is idempotent for the same workflow_id and run_id.

edge_cases.criterion: Concurrent workflows and retries write isolated artifacts
edge_cases.gherkin: Given multiple workflow runs and activity retries execute concurrently, when logs, ATIF exports, and reports are written, then each artifact is scoped to the correct workflow_id, run_id, activity, and attempt with no overwrite or metric mixing.

edge_cases.criterion: Unauthorized, stale, duplicate, or contradictory human signals
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a workflow is awaiting human input, when an unauthorized caller or a stale, duplicate, or contradictory signal is received, then it is rejected or ignored deterministically and cannot alter an already consumed or terminal decision.

edge_cases.criterion: Operator session or client disconnects while the workflow awaits a decision
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the operator client disconnects or its session expires while the durable workflow awaits a decision, when the client reconnects with authorization, then it can query the current state and submit one valid decision before timeout without losing the escalation context.

edge_cases.criterion: Cadence or worker unavailable, activity timeout, or network interruption
edge_cases.gherkin: Given Cadence, a worker, or network communication is unavailable during a step, when retry and timeout policies are exhausted, then the workflow remains durable, records attempts accurately, and reaches the configured automated-failure or human-escalation path without a false success report.

edge_cases.criterion: Devin invocation fails, times out, or is rate limited
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the Devin harness fails, times out, or is rate limited, when activity retry policy executes, then every attempt is separately logged and the final report records the terminal activity outcome without counting failed attempts as successful workflow runs.

edge_cases.criterion: ATIF export is absent, malformed, incomplete, or omits cost_usd
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a completed harness invocation has no readable ATIF export or omits one or more usage fields, when reporting runs, then the report preserves available raw evidence, marks unavailable normalized values explicitly, does not invent cost, and records a diagnostic without discarding the workflow outcome.

edge_cases.criterion: Maximum repair count and exact signal-timeout boundary
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the configured repair limit is reached or a signal arrives exactly at the timeout boundary, when the engine evaluates the next transition, then only one deterministic terminal or escalation transition occurs and the report contains no extra attempt or duplicate human decision.

edge_cases.criterion: Report or log destination is unwritable or storage is exhausted
edge_cases.gherkin: Given the configured artifact destination rejects a write or has insufficient capacity, when logging or report generation occurs, then certification evidence is not reported as complete and the failure is surfaced through an available independent channel or workflow result.

questions.question: What exact Stage 4 end-to-end success formula is authoritative: non-failed terminal runs, fully automated passed runs, or both as separate metrics?
What sample size, workload mix, and observation window qualify as representative and demonstrate stability or improvement over time?
Does Stage 3 require each agent's individual score and manual-correction rate to meet 95%, and how is a manual correction distinguished from an intentional punch-out?
Should ACTIVITY_FLAGGED_AMBIGUITY be raised by a structured activity result, a dedicated adversarial guardrail, an exception, or more than one mechanism?
What independent adversarial-review behavior and pass/fail contract satisfy the requirement to challenge prior outputs without duplicating grade_story_analysis?
What authentication and authorization mechanism identifies callers allowed to send human_response signals?
Should a report be emitted for startup rejection, cancellation, timeout, and infrastructure failure, or only for terminal workflow results?
When ATIF omits total_cost_usd, should cost_usd be null with an availability reason, derived from a versioned price table, or supplied by an updated harness contract?
Where should consolidated reports and benchmark summaries be stored, and what service owns retention and cleanup?
What maximum source size, path length, attempt count, and report history size must be supported?
